dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: This defines the m-by-n matrix E entrywise by E_ij = ((YR)_ij - A_ij) + ((DeltaY R)_ij + ((Y DeltaR)_ij + (DeltaY DeltaR)_ij)). By distributivity, E = (Y + DeltaY)(R + DeltaR) - A.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the matrix whose operator action is bounded in the conclusion.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is ordinary finite matrix multiplication: for an m-by-n matrix B and an n-by-p matrix C, (BC)_ij = sum over k in Fin n of B_ik C_kj.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It defines YR, DeltaY R, Y DeltaR, and DeltaY DeltaR, including the base residual YR - A.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003
dependency_coverage.meaning: For an m-by-n real matrix B and real c, this is the proposition that for every x in R^n, ||Bx||_2 <= c||x||_2.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It interprets every matrix hypothesis and the conclusion as a uniform Euclidean operator-bound inequality; it does not assert that c equals the operator norm.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef004
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is matrix-vector multiplication: for an m-by-n matrix B and x in R^n, (Bx)_i = sum over j in Fin n of B_ij x_j.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It specifies the matrix action appearing inside every bound represented by LocalDef003.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef005
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the Euclidean norm of a finite real vector: ||x||_2 = sqrt(sum over i in Fin n of x_i^2).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies both the output and input norms in all hypotheses and in the conclusion.

dependency_coverage.name: Fin
dependency_coverage.meaning: Fin q is the finite index type consisting of the natural-number indices below q.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It gives the row, column, and summation index sets and thereby fixes all matrix and vector dimensions.

dependency_coverage.name: HAdd.hAdd
dependency_coverage.meaning: This projects the addition operation supplied by an HAdd instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: With the supplied real instances, every occurrence is ordinary real addition, including entrywise matrix-expression addition and addition in the final scalar bound.

dependency_coverage.name: HMul.hMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: This projects the multiplication operation supplied by an HMul instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: With the supplied real instances, every occurrence is ordinary real multiplication in matrix products, matrix-vector products, norm bounds, and the scalar expression.

dependency_coverage.name: HSub.hSub
dependency_coverage.meaning: This projects the subtraction operation supplied by an HSub instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: With the real subtraction instance, it makes the base residual entry equal to (YR)_ij - A_ij.

dependency_coverage.name: LE.le
dependency_coverage.meaning: This projects the binary order relation supplied by an LE instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: With the real-order instance, it interprets all displayed inequalities as ordinary non-strict real inequalities.

dependency_coverage.name: Nat
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the type of natural numbers, including zero.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The dimensions m and n may be any finite natural dimensions, including zero-dimensional cases.

dependency_coverage.name: OfNat.ofNat
dependency_coverage.meaning: This converts a natural-number literal to the corresponding value supplied by an OfNat instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It interprets the literal 0 in the explicit nonnegativity assumptions as real zero and participates in interpreting numerical literals used by the definitions.

dependency_coverage.name: Real
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the type of real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: All matrix entries, vector entries, constants, operations, norms, and inequalities are real-valued.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instAdd
dependency_coverage.meaning: This supplies ordinary addition on the real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It fixes all real additions in the residual matrix and scalar error bound to be standard real addition.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instLE
dependency_coverage.meaning: This supplies the usual order relation on the real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes heY and hy the assumptions 0 <= eY and 0 <= y and gives the usual order in each norm inequality.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: This supplies ordinary multiplication on the real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It fixes products of entries and products of scalar bounds to be standard real multiplication.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instSub
dependency_coverage.meaning: This supplies real subtraction, defined as addition of the additive inverse.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It gives the exact residual term YR - A.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instZero
dependency_coverage.meaning: This supplies the additive identity 0 of the real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It fixes the zero in the assumptions 0 <= eY and 0 <= y and the zero values arising from empty sums.

dependency_coverage.name: Zero.toOfNat0
dependency_coverage.meaning: This turns a Zero instance into the interpretation of the numeral 0.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It ensures that the literal 0 used in the real inequalities is precisely real zero.

dependency_coverage.name: instHAdd
dependency_coverage.meaning: This lifts a homogeneous Add operation on a type to the corresponding HAdd operation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Together with Real.instAdd, it resolves all heterogeneous-addition notation here to ordinary addition of real numbers.

dependency_coverage.name: instHMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: This lifts a homogeneous Mul operation on a type to the corresponding HMul operation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Together with Real.instMul, it resolves all multiplication notation here to ordinary multiplication of real numbers.

dependency_coverage.name: instHSub
dependency_coverage.meaning: This lifts a homogeneous Sub operation on a type to the corresponding HSub operation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Together with Real.instSub, it resolves the subtraction in YR - A to ordinary real subtraction.

dependency_coverage.name: Fin.fintype
dependency_coverage.meaning: This equips Fin q with a finite enumeration containing every index exactly once.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It permits universal finite sums over all row, column, and inner-product indices, including empty sums when q = 0.

dependency_coverage.name: Finset.sum
dependency_coverage.meaning: This forms the finite sum of a function over a finite set using the additive commutative monoid operation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It defines all matrix products, matrix-vector products, and sums of coordinate squares.

dependency_coverage.name: Finset.univ
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a finite type, this is the finite set containing all of its elements.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes every sum in the definitions range over every index of the appropriate Fin type.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instAddCommMonoid
dependency_coverage.meaning: This supplies the additive commutative monoid structure of the real numbers, including associative and commutative addition and zero.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It provides the operation used by finite real sums and makes an empty finite sum equal to zero.

dependency_coverage.name: HPow.hPow
dependency_coverage.meaning: This projects the exponentiation operation supplied by an HPow instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: In the Euclidean norm definition, it interprets each coordinate expression x_i^2.

dependency_coverage.name: Monoid.toNatPow
dependency_coverage.meaning: This supplies natural-number exponentiation in a monoid by repeated multiplication.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: For real numbers and exponent 2, it makes x_i^2 the ordinary square x_i x_i.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instMonoid
dependency_coverage.meaning: This supplies the multiplicative monoid structure of the real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It underlies natural powers of real coordinates in the Euclidean norm.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.sqrt
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the nonnegative real square-root operation; its definition extends square root to all reals through the nonnegative part.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It turns the nonnegative sum of coordinate squares into the ordinary Euclidean norm.

dependency_coverage.name: instHPow
dependency_coverage.meaning: This lifts a Pow operation to the corresponding HPow operation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Together with natural real powers, it resolves the coordinate exponentiation in x_i^2.

dependency_coverage.name: instOfNatNat
dependency_coverage.meaning: This interprets each natural-number literal n as the natural number n itself.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes the exponent literal 2 in the norm definition exactly the natural number two.

binders: m and n are universally quantified natural numbers.
Y, DeltaY, and A are universally quantified real m-by-n matrices, represented as functions Fin m -> Fin n -> Real.
R and DeltaR are universally quantified real n-by-n matrices, represented as functions Fin n -> Fin n -> Real.
e0, eY, r, y, and eR are universally quantified real constants.
Within each matrix-bound hypothesis and within the conclusion, the vector x is independently universally quantified over R^n; there are no existentially quantified witnesses.
hypotheses: For every x in R^n, ||(YR - A)x||_2 <= e0||x||_2.
For every x in R^n, ||DeltaY x||_2 <= eY||x||_2.
For every x in R^n, ||R x||_2 <= r||x||_2.
For every x in R^n, ||Y x||_2 <= y||x||_2.
For every x in R^n, ||DeltaR x||_2 <= eR||x||_2.
conclusions: For every x in R^n, ||Ex||_2 <= (e0 + (eY r + (y eR + eY eR)))||x||_2, where E = (YR - A) + (DeltaY R + (Y DeltaR + DeltaY DeltaR)), equivalently E = (Y + DeltaY)(R + DeltaR) - A.
mathematical_definitions: For B in R^(m-by-n) and C in R^(n-by-p), (BC)_ij = sum from k in Fin n of B_ik C_kj.
For B in R^(m-by-n) and x in R^n, (Bx)_i = sum from j in Fin n of B_ij x_j.
For x in R^q, ||x||_2 = sqrt(sum from i in Fin q of x_i^2), using the nonnegative square root.
The predicate represented by LocalDef003(B,c) means exactly that ||Bx||_2 <= c||x||_2 for every x in the domain of B.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For arbitrary finite-dimensional real matrices of the stated dimensions, suppose eY and y are nonnegative and e0, eY, r, y, and eR respectively provide uniform Euclidean operator bounds for YR - A, DeltaY, R, Y, and DeltaR. Then the expanded perturbed residual (Y + DeltaY)(R + DeltaR) - A has the uniform Euclidean operator bound e0 + eY r + y eR + eY eR.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The dimensions m and n may be zero; no positivity assumption on either dimension is encoded.

If n = 0, the only input vector is the empty vector, all relevant matrix-vector products and norms are zero, every LocalDef003 bound is automatically 0 <= 0, and the conclusion is automatic regardless of the bound constants, subject only to the separately supplied assumptions 0 <= eY and 0 <= y.

If n > 0, any hypothesis LocalDef003(B,c) forces c >= 0 because it must hold for a vector with positive Euclidean norm. Thus negative choices of e0, r, or eR make their corresponding premises impossible and the implication vacuous, even though their nonnegativity is not stated separately.
The constants are only upper-bound certificates. The proposition does not assert that any of e0, eY, r, y, or eR equals an induced operator norm or is a minimal bound.
Only finite-dimensional real matrices and the Euclidean vector norm are represented.

No invertibility, nonsingularity, triangularity, orthogonality, rank condition, relative-error condition, floating-point model, algorithmic origin, or relationship between the perturbations and computed quantities is encoded beyond the displayed dimensions and norm bounds.
The conclusion is one uniform matrix-action bound; it does not provide entrywise bounds, lower bounds, equality, or an existential construction.
